title: Grandparents' background and her own name, Francis M.
summary: Grandfather Creole, grandmother white; she explains Mimi Francis and the M for Mouton.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: Did you say after your grandmother, you were telling your grandfather Creole and your grandmother white, or how was it?

No, my grandmother was white, and my grandfather was a Creole, my mother's father. And my grandmother's second marriage, she married a Portuguese. His name was Ardway Chalut. Her last two children were for this Portuguese. I mean, Papa Joey, as we called him, because his name was Ardway Chalute. I wouldn't know how to spell that.
No, I wouldn't either. Portuguese names would be hard to spell.
Did you cut that thing off? No, it's going on. Is that so? It's going on.

Well. I had it off there for a while. But your grandmother's name— Excuse me, I just don't use the breakdown. No, that's all right. I understand. I certainly understand. Your grandmother's name then was Mimi, too. No, my great-grandmother's name was Mimi, yes. But your name then really was Mimi named after her. Yes, I am. Mimi Francis was your— That's right. But you dropped the Mimi.

Well, I don't—you know, I put Francis M. Oliver all the time. And the M's can either be for Mimi or Mouton. That's what I thought it was for the Mouton. Yes, it is for the Mouton. Because I never have dropped my father's name. Yes.
